newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore PM says had to sue opposition politicians.
newsitem.headline: Singapore PM says had to sue opposition politicians.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong was quoted on Sunday as saying that he had to sue opposition politicians to preserve his integrity.
Goh was reported in The Sunday Times of Singapore as saying, "Once you are defamed, of course you have to make sure that the truth comes out. That means I have to sue him."
Goh was referring specifically to his latest suit which is against veteran Workers' Party opposition leader Joshua Jeyaretnam.
Goh has also issued a series of writs against Workers' Party politician Tang Liang Hong alleging defamation.
He said he had had to sue Tang because a lawsuit was his only defence. Goh said Tang had defamed him, called him a liar and accused him of criminal defamation.
"If Tang Liang Hong calls me a liar and I don't sue, then I'll be in the same class as Chee Soon Juan, so I have no choice but to sue him," the Sunday Times quoted Goh as saying.
Chee Soon Juan is a leader of the opposition Democratic Party who is a frequent subject of ruling People's Action Party (PAP) attacks.

The Sunday Times said Goh was responding to reporters' questions on whether the PAP was concerned about any adverse public reaction to the recent spate of lawsuits and whether such action was seen as a move to 'get' Tang.
Goh said, "There'll be some public sympathy for him, but the matter is for the court to decide."

Tang was an unsuccessful candidate in a hotly contested constituency in Singapore's general election on January 2. He left Singapore shortly after the election, saying he had received death threats. He is in London.
The PAP won 81 out of the 83 seats contested.

Worker's Party leader Jeyaretnam was beaten in the election but will take a seat in parliament anyway under a constitutional provision for a seat for best-loser if only two opposition members are elected to parliament.
